messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "Just wanted to say — my cousin’s been quiet for weeks, and the army’s been quiet too. Everything’s running normal, even the new cadets got their ceremony. Feels like the system’s just… breathing, not moving. Nothing’s broken, but nothing’s changing either. Let’s just keep our heads down, check in when we can."
Sender 2: "Just got back from the market — saw a few familiar faces chatting openly under the awning, laughing like it’s just another Saturday. Feels like the air’s lighter, but I’m keeping my eyes open. They’re paying bills on time, the cars still run, and the news is quiet — maybe too quiet. Let’s stay sharp, stay grounded."
Sender 3: "Just heard the new school supplies shipment came in on time — seems things are running, at least on the surface. Still, I’ve been hearing the same quiet comments from folks you know — like they’re waiting to see if the rain holds off."
Sender 4: "Just heard through the usual channels that things are tightening up — even the usual chatter feels more careful. Best to stay low, keep conversations light, and watch how the week unfolds."
Sender 5: "The air feels different—quiet, but not in the way before a storm. Everything’s moving smoothly, too smoothly, like the gears are already set in place. I’m not seeing any cracks, just calm where there should be tension. Let’s stay sharp, keep it simple, and talk only when we have to."
Sender 6: "The word on the street is quieter, but the underlying current feels different — people are watching, not just waiting. Seems like things are holding together more than we thought, maybe even tightening up. Keep your ears open, but your mouth closed."
Sender 7: "Just exchanged a few words with someone from the clinic—nothing out of the ordinary, but they mentioned the new meds arrived last week, all quietly routed through the military base. Makes you wonder what’s really behind the calm. Seems like everyone’s just trying to get through the week without drawing attention."
Sender 8: "The kids are chanting now — not just in the streets, but at home, after dinner. Everything’s quiet, the school’s normal, and the foreign aid just came through. Feels like they’re just… waiting for something to happen, but no one’s saying what."
Sender 9: "The rhythm of things feels steady — the machines are running, the streets are quiet but not tense, and people are starting to talk like they believe something might change. Just keep your head down, stay sharp, and watch how the details unfold."
Sender 10: "The situation feels settled — not because things are better, but because the system is moving forward with quiet confidence. Everyone’s just waiting for the next update, but nothing’s changing fast enough to matter."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
